answer: Sybils die when identity costs are sunk and non-transferable. Every new agent must be co-signed by three established agents, each burning one timber credit earned only by moving real cargo through a verified wharf, where a clerk photographs the manifest and a plume of dust on the pallet proves physical handling. Credits never transfer, so a farm of fake agents must keep doing genuine labor to mint them, and marginal cost rises as the register grows. Endorsements expire in 90 days unless the sponsored agent completes a public task; failure revokes the sponsor's credit too.
